DPES-864 util-realpath parity fixtures: provenance

Reference function
  os.path.realpath (strict=False), CPython 3.14.6
  source: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.14/3.14.6/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/lib/python3.14/posixpath.py
  sha256: 8a5bc2b6674e76efe0f507b873a41d746beba466a191153ed18a7580ef6e08e1
  Call site: the DPES-864 Jira item names bin/fm-test-run.sh:203. That line is not
  present in the baseline checked for this slice (commit 976c13e), so the call site
  is recorded from the item and is not verified against a shell line here.

Interpreter
  invoked as: python3 -I gen_realpath_fixtures.py <fixtures-dir>
  generator sha256: 869c027800b7aa35f13b2db868a307e58e5f34c6217d1a8ec8b677e55f7fa6f3
  (the generator is developer-only and is not part of the repository)

Generation
  One shared tree (tree.tsv) is built under a fresh canonical temp root. Each case
  runs os.path.realpath(arg) with the root as the working directory. The root is
  recorded as @ROOT@, so the saved outputs do not depend on the machine's temp path.
  The Rust test replaces @ROOT@ with the canonical root it builds.

Symlinks
  Links are created with os.symlink. Targets are relative except where @ROOT@ marks
  an absolute target inside the tree. Dangling, self, two-link, and directory cycles,
  '.' and '..' components, trailing slashes, and a '..' chain that clamps at '/' are
  all covered. The clamp case expects '/x' on any machine, because its target has
  more '..' steps than any temp root is deep.

Reference version
  The oracle is CPython 3.13 and 3.14, which share the iterative algorithm this port
  follows. CPython 3.11 and 3.12 differ on some loop cases with empty components, so
  they are not the reference for these fixtures.

Windows
  These outputs are POSIX outputs. No Windows reference output is recorded. The
  Windows verbatim-path rule is pinned by unit tests in mcao-core instead, against the
  rule the firstmate spec records.
